title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day on campus.


MDS moves fast. Orientation week was hectic, but super fun at the same time. I did ask myself “What did I get myself into quite a few times” but week one made me realise I was exactly where I’m supposed to be.
Making friends was easy, Cohort 11 has some super cool people. I was fascinated to learn that MDS this year has students from 35+ nationalities. I dont think I have ever been in a room with such diversity.
Coming out of a whirlwind of team-building exercises, technical workshops, and wellness sessions, both the cohort and I are fully primed to tackle the challenges ahead!

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
By default, R might try to use your system’s global Python. To ensure true reproducibility, we explicitly tell the reticulate package to use the Python binary inside our uv virtual environment.

library(reticulate)

# Force reticulate to use the project's .venv
use_virtualenv("../../.venv", required = TRUE)

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Creating Data in R
First, let’s create a simple dataframe using R.

# Create a small dataset in R
r_data <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  score = c(85, 92, 78, 90, 88)
)
print(r_data)

  id score
1  1    85
2  2    92
3  3    78
4  4    90
5  5    88

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Reading R Data into Python
Now, we switch to a Python chunk. We can read the R object natively into Python by calling r.name (where “name” is the variable we created in R).

import pandas as pd

# Access the R dataframe using r.r_data
python_df = r.r_data

# Modify the dataframe using Python (adding a curve to the score)
python_df['curved_score'] = python_df['score'] + 5
print(python_df)

   id  score  curved_score
0   1   85.0          90.0
1   2   92.0          97.0
2   3   78.0          83.0
3   4   90.0          95.0
4   5   88.0          93.0

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
section: Returning Python Data back to R
text:
Returning Python Data back to R
Finally, we switch back to an R chunk. We can retrieve the modified dataframe from Python by calling py$name.

# Access the modified Python dataframe using py$python_df
final_r_data <- py$python_df

# Display the curved scores back in R
print(final_r_data)

  id score curved_score
1  1    85           90
2  2    92           97
3  3    78           83
4  4    90           95
5  5    88           93
